observations: A blocky face shape sits against a flat medium-blue field; thick black outlines divide the form into horizontal slab-like sections from brow to chin.
Two asymmetric eye zones—left roughly almond-shaped, right more rectangular—are filled with looping red and yellow lines over dark cores, giving each a different internal rhythm.
Dense short multicolor strokes in yellow, red, pink, cyan, and green cover every surface, while white highlight lines run along the outer edges of each slab, suggesting volume.
reading: The face reads as a stack of compressed planes rather than a continuous surface, each band holding its own color pressure. The two eye zones pull in opposite directions—one coiled inward, one cross-hatched outward—so the face feels split between two moods at once. That tension sits quietly against the even blue ground, which offers no drama of its own, leaving the internal line noise to carry the weight.
contextAngle: Within the owned nifty-faces subset, this work shares the flat blue ground of title neighbor nnxyz nifty faces #42, but trades that work's open circular eyes and wide tooth-filled mouth for compressed horizontal slabs and a tighter, closed expression. Title and recorded-creation order align for this work.

connections.reason: Both works place a blocky face on a blue ground with dense multicolor line fill, but nnxyz nifty faces #42 uses large circular eye rings and an open tooth-filled mouth, while this work compresses the face into horizontal slabs with narrower, asymmetric eyes—a direct contrast in openness versus compression.

lookingQuestion: The two eye zones use different internal line patterns—what does that difference do to how you read the left side of the face versus the right?
ambiguities: nnxyz rawblocks #22 shares the same artist and a blue ground but differs enough in form, mark density, and collection that no strong formal connection to this work is visible beyond background color; omitted.
Title order and recorded-creation order coincide for this work, but the metadata notes gaps may exist elsewhere in the family, so sequence position is not confirmed as strict making order.
